claims: As of April 1, 2026, the Artemis II mission successfully launched.
As of April 1, 2026, the Orion spacecraft is currently in a high Earth orbit.
The crew of the Artemis II mission consists of four astronauts.
The crew of the Artemis II mission will spend roughly 24 hours in high Earth orbit before proceeding to the Moon.
The Artemis II mission is a 10-day mission.
The crew of the Artemis II mission is performing system checks.
As of late April 1, 2026, the crew of the Artemis II mission is beginning to prepare for proximity operations.
As of April 1-2, 2026, the Artemis II is in Earth orbit after a successful launch from Kennedy Space Center at 6:35 p.m. EDT.
The Artemis II launched from Kennedy Space Center at 6:35 p.m. EDT.
The crew of the Artemis II mission will conduct a 70-minute proximity operations test.
The proximity operations test involves maneuvering the Orion capsule near the expended Upper Stage rocket.
Following the proximity operations tests, the Orion spacecraft will perform an engine burn to transition from Earth orbit to a trajectory toward the Moon.
The Artemis II mission is a 10-day crewed test flight to circle the Moon and return.
The Artemis II mission marks the first human mission to the lunar vicinity since 1972.
